beats.care: Buying Deepavali sweets? Check the FSSAI licence number on the box, and avoid loose sweets kept in the open.
beats.what: TG SAFE inspected 21 sweet units, seized food worth ₹7.76 lakh and suspended three shops' FSSAI licences.
beats.why: Officials found cockroaches, rat droppings, expired items and non-food-grade rose water. One shop had 705 kg seized.

cards.body: Shops in Kukatpally, Masab Tank and Chandanagar had licences suspended; one in Tarnaka was shut for having no licence. 21 samples were sent for testing.
Update (Oct 25): TG SAFE issued improvement notices to 20 sweet shops and manufacturing units, and a show-cause notice to one more, after statewide inspections found hygiene violations.
For selling habit-forming drugs without prescriptions, in a separate drive.
cards.caption: Medical shops whose licences were suspended

cards.body: At one shop, sweets were covered with curtains and newspapers.

cards.q: Where will you buy sweets this Deepavali?
Which body raided the sweet shops?
cards.why: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) ran the drive.

hook: Before Deepavali, *1,035 kg* of sweets and ghee seized in Hyderabad

learn.t: Every food business must display an FSSAI licence or registration number; you can verify it on FSSAI's website.
